Introduction This Scope of Work (SOW) outlines the requirements, deliverables, and implementation plan for the replacement of interpretive panels at the Minidoka Historic Site Visitor Contact Station. 2. Project Background The Issei Memorial exhibit was donated to the park by Friends of Minidoka (FOM) and created with support from a Japanese American Confinement Sites grant and contributions from community members. It honors the Issei, the immigrant generation incarcerated at Minidoka, through interpretive panels and a memorial wall featuring the n

the names of more than 4,400 Issei who were incarcerated at Minidoka. 3. Project Objectives Over the past five years, visitors and community members have found spelling mistakes, errors, and missing names on this Issei Memorial Wall. This project will update and correct these errors through the research, design, fabrication and delivery of three polycarbonate exhibit panels (62in x 44in). The new panels will be installed on the already existing base made of historic WWII camp wood. The design and fabrication of the wall shall include the printing of the corrected information. Contractor will produce a finished exhibit. o 3.2 Deliverables 1. Three (3) Double Sided – 62” x 44” polycarbonate exhibit panels printed with the corrected information as provided by NPS. 2.
